summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of prior stents presented with severe substernal chest pain radiating to the right arm, occurring at rest and relieved partially by nitroglycerin. Initial evaluation revealed a mildly elevated troponin, consistent with unstable angina. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which showed in-stent restenosis in the mid-distal right coronary artery, and successfully received a drug-eluting stent. During the hospitalization, he experienced transient hyperkalemia corrected with dialysis and had a self-limited episode of guaiac-positive dark stools with a transient drop in hemoglobin, managed with pantoprazole. His blood pressure was managed with adjustment of isosorbide mononitrate. He remained stable, completed scheduled dialysis, and was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy, optimized cardiac medications, and instructions for outpatient follow-up including endoscopy and cardiology evaluation.
